attributes.proposal_description:
<Background and Context>

Nigeria stands at the forefront of Africa’s crypto revolution. According to the 2023 Chainalysis report, the country leads the continent in cryptocurrency activity and ranks second globally in the Global Crypto Adoption Index. Notably, despite market volatility and economic uncertainty, Nigeria’s crypto economy recorded a 9.0% growth rate, placing it third among the top 50 countries worldwide

This momentum is driven largely by the country’s youthful population, many of whom have turned to cryptocurrencies like BTC and USDT as a hedge against inflation and currency depreciation. A recent study by Nigeria’s leading exchange, Busha, revealed that one in three users prefers USDT, making it the second most-used crypto asset after BTC. This widespread adoption of stablecoins demonstrates a strong foundation of trust, and sets the stage for the introduction of USDA, a Cardano-native stablecoin

More broadly, Sub-Saharan Africa continues to face systemic barriers to financial access—especially around cross-border payments and capital preservation. The World Bank reports that the average cost of sending money to the region is 8%, with some countries experiencing even higher fees: 19% in Nigeria, 13.9% in Kenya, and 27% in Tanzania. These high costs, combined with growing remittance flows and currency instability, have created strong demand for alternative financial tools that are secure, affordable, and accessible.

Meanwhile, innovative fintech platforms such as Ejara and Nestcoin are emerging as trusted interfaces for users across the continent. Ejara, active across Francophone Africa, allows users to buy crypto and save in decentralized wallets, giving them mobile-based access to long-term savings tools and even tokenized government bonds. Nestcoin, through its Onboard wallet, is building a gateway into Web3 for everyday users by combining payments, custody, and soon—yield opportunities.

However, ADA and USDA—the key native assets of Cardano—are still underrepresented across these platforms. ADA remains listed on only a limited number of exchanges, with low liquidity and limited trading activity, while USDA has yet to be integrated at all. This gap between Cardano’s technology stack and real-world access points has hindered adoption.

Our proposal, ADA/USDA Liquidity Improvement, aims to close this gap through targeted integration with trusted African fintechs and exchanges. By embedding USDA into platforms like Busha, Ejara, and Nestcoin, and by expanding liquidity for ADA across local markets, we can enable Cardano-native assets to serve real-world financial needs—from remittances and savings to DeFi access and yield.

<Proposal Overview>

This 12-month initiative—ADA/USDA Liquidity Improvement—aims to strategically enhance the liquidity and adoption of ADA and USDA across African exchanges, DeFi protocols, and fintech platforms. By deepening partnerships with local fintechs and remittance providers, this project will turn Cardano-native assets into practical financial tools across the continent.

<How This Works – A Simple End-to-End Flow>

To make this initiative easy to understand at a glance, the following flow shows how the ADA/USDA Liquidity Improvement proposal will function in practice—from partner integration to real-world usage and value return to the Cardano ecosystem:

1. Partnership Integration
 → Integrate ADA and USDA into trusted local fintech platforms and exchanges:
 – Busha (Nigeria)
 – Ejara (Francophone Africa)
 – Nestcoin / Onboard (Nigeria and Kenya)


2. User Onboarding via Local Channels
 → Users buy or receive USDA through local fiat onramps (e.g., mobile money, bank transfer)
 → Platforms educate users on how to save, send, and store USDA


3. Usage in Real-World Financial Activities
 → Users utilize USDA for:
 – Low-cost remittances
 – Stable savings/investments
 – Access to tokenized bonds and USD-based products


4. Connection to Cardano DeFi Ecosystem
 → Fintech apps connect to DeFi protocols on Cardano
 → Users can:
 – Lend or stake USDA
 – Earn yield
 – Swap assets


5. Value Returned to Cardano Ecosystem
 → Increased on-chain activity, ADA/USDA liquidity, and user base
 → Greater exposure for Cardano across African markets
 → Sustainable adoption of decentralized financial tools

<Strategic Pillars>

1. Stablecoin Integration and Cross-Border Access (Busha & Ejara)

- Partner with Busha (Nigeria) and Ejara (Francophone Africa) to list USDA and enable stable, dollar-backed access to crypto through local fiat onramps (e.g., mobile money, bank transfers).


- Build regional remittance corridors using USDA for cost-efficient, borderless transfers among diaspora and local recipients.（Ejara’s non-custodial investment and savings functionality positions it as a key stablecoin distribution channel for underbanked users in Francophone Africa.）

- Launch educational and onboarding campaigns focused on savings, remittance, and financial protection using USDA.


2. Retail Financial Empowerment through Fintech Channels

- Work with platforms like Nestcoin to make USDA accessible to users directly within their wallets.


- Enable access to savings, investment, and tokenized bond products via blockchain rails.


- Provide communities with low-threshold entry points into digital finance, especially for users impacted by inflation and currency instability.


3. Unlocking Cardano-native DeFi Access and Yield

- Bridge users to Cardano-native DeFi protocols through one-click integration of USDA in fintech apps.


- Enable secure lending, staking, and yield farming powered by USDA, making DeFi accessible to everyday users.


- Collaborate with local partners to ensure KYC-compliant off-ramps via trusted wallets and payment providers.

attributes.key_proposal_deliverables:
<Key Deliverables and Definitions of Done>

The following quarterly roadmap outlines the strategic rollout and impact delivery of the ADA/USDA liquidity initiative across a 12-month timeline. Each phase is designed to build progressively—from laying the foundational partnerships and integrations, to launching USDA in production environments, enabling real-world use cases, and scaling adoption across key African markets. Tangible outputs and performance indicators are captured through quarterly impact reports, ensuring continuous transparency and adaptive execution.

<ADA Liquidity Expansion>

 ADA is successfully listed and liquidity is deployed on leading African exchanges. Success is defined by a measurable increase in daily trading volume compared to the pre-initiative baseline.


- USDA Integration into Exchange, Remittance, and Fintech Applications
 USDA is fully integrated into at least two live fintech platforms (e.g., Ejara, Nestcoin, Busha), with over 10,000 USDA wallets created or users onboarded through these platforms.


- Real-World Use Cases Enabled
 Users are able to use USDA for practical financial activities such as remittances, savings, and tokenized bond investments directly through partner platform interfaces. These use cases are demonstrably active in at least two different African countries.


- Cardano-native DeFi Access
 More than 1,000 users engage with DeFi functionalities—such as staking, lending, and yield generation—through USDA-enabled wallets like Onboard by Nestcoin, showcasing Cardano’s accessible DeFi layer.


- Ecosystem Awareness and Education
 In partnership with local ecosystem players, a minimum of 10 educational events are conducted across at least three countries. Educational content is localized and disseminated through partner channels to ensure regional relevance and accessibility.


- Quarterly Impact Reports
 Comprehensive quarterly reports are produced, detailing progress on adoption, liquidity metrics, partner engagement, and community feedback. These reports provide transparency and inform ongoing strategy adjustments.

<Quarter-by-quarter milestones>

Quarter 1: Foundation & Integration 
- Partnership agreement finalized
- Technical integration of USDA initiated
- Liquidity planning & MM strategy defined
- First community events hosted
-Q1 Report Delivered

Quarter 2: Launch & Early Adoption
- USDA live on at least 2 platforms
- USDA/Fiat or USDA/ADA pairs live
- 2,500+ USDA retail users onboarded
- DeFi integration MVP launched
- 3+ ecosystem events held
- Q2 Report Delivered

Quarter 3: Expansion & Yield Access
- USDA-enabled DeFi live & active
- Tokenized RWA pilot launched
- 10+ liquidity education events hosted
- Cross-border remittance pilot launched
- 7,500+ USDA users across platforms
- Q3 Report Delivered

Quarter 4: Consolidation & Scale
- 10,000 USDA users reached
- USDA volume milestone hit
- 3 exchanges/wallets support USDA
- 1–2 additional DeFi or savings products added
- Final community showcase + impact summary
- Final Year-End Impact Report

attributes.problem_statement:
Despite ADA being listed on several prominent African exchanges—including Luno, VALR, Busha, Yellow Card, and Quidax—its trading volume and liquidity remain significantly underdeveloped. Key structural challenges persist: limited incentives for users, lack of stablecoin pairing, and the absence of institutional liquidity providers have slowed ecosystem growth and DeFi adoption.

Meanwhile, Cardano’s native stablecoin, USDA, is not yet integrated into any major African exchange or fintech platform, despite increasing demand for stable, dollar-denominated assets driven by inflation, currency devaluation, and rising remittance flows. This gap severely limits the Cardano ecosystem’s ability to deliver practical financial solutions in regions where it is needed most.

While Cardano's long-term vision is to empower developing nations through decentralized infrastructure, four key challenges currently prevent this mission from being realized in Africa:

- Insufficient liquidity for ADA and USDA, discouraging market participation by both retail users and liquidity providers.


- Lack of real-world integration and enterprise use cases for Cardano-based stablecoins, weakening the bridge between technology and everyday economic activity.


- No accessible, yield-generating, dollar-based products for users in inflation-hit, low-yield African economies—despite growing familiarity with USDT and USDC.


- A fragmented user journey, with most people in emerging markets having no clear onramp or incentive to engage with the Cardano ecosystem.


This proposal aims to solve these bottlenecks through a real-world-first, integration-driven approach, leveraging trusted local fintech players like Busha, Ejara, and Nestcoin. By expanding liquidity, enabling stablecoin infrastructure, and connecting Cardano DeFi to active user bases, we can turn latent demand into meaningful economic participation.
attributes.proposal_benefit:
If implemented, this proposal will deliver the following benefits to both the Cardano ecosystem and real-world communities in Africa:

- Boost ADA liquidity and trading volume by collaborating with leading African exchanges such as Busha, driving institutional-grade market-making and broader retail participation through improved price stability and trading incentives.


- Introduce USDA as a trusted, dollar-pegged stablecoin across remittance-focused apps and fintech platforms including Ejara and Nestcoin, enabling secure, low-cost cross-border payments and savings—especially for users affected by currency devaluation.


- Bridge Cardano DeFi with active user bases by embedding ADA/USDA access into consumer-facing wallets and platforms, unlocking real utility via lending, swapping, and stable yield generation, powered by the Cardano stack.


- Facilitate onboarding and financial education via regional community hubs, integrating wallet tools, user training, and localized support to scale adoption sustainably and inclusively.


ROI for the Cardano Community includes:
- Substantial increase in transaction volume and TVL (total value locked) as Cardano-native assets are adopted across high-need, high-growth African markets.


- Meaningful growth in DeFi participation from previously untapped user segments, driven by real economic needs (remittances, saving, yield-seeking).


- Tangible expansion of ADA and USDA use in day-to-day finance, increasing network stickiness and long-term value capture.


- Increased developer and enterprise engagement in Africa, leading to deeper Cardano infrastructure integration and broader ecosystem resilience.

attributes.comment_text:
1. How will the KPI of 10,000 USDA users be validated and measured? Will metrics such as retention rate and active usage per user also be reported?

2. While quarterly impact reports are listed as a KPI, what are the criteria, format, and disclosure channels for these reports?

3. The KPI of “1,000+ users engaging in DeFi” — which protocols and specific activities (e.g., staking, lending) will be counted? What qualifies a user as a “DeFi participant” among the 1,000+ KPI? Does it involve only wallet connections or verifiable transactions over time?

4. Has this proposal been adequately socialized across Cardano community platforms such as X, Discord, Reddit, and the Forum? What feedback has been received? Given that the Q&A section has no comments and only a few votes have been cast, is there a risk that this proposal is perceived as under-socialized?

5. Is there verifiable support from the African Cardano community, such as event recordings, social media engagement, or endorsements from fintech partners?

6. ₳60,000 is allocated for “DeFi/RWA Product Pilots” — what specific real-world asset (RWA) use cases will be piloted, and where?

7. The outsourcing budget includes ₳216,000 for project management — is this an external vendor or an internal role? Who will be contracted and what are the deliverables?

8. After the 12-month program ends, how will ADA/USDA liquidity and user engagement be sustained without continued treasury funding?

9. There appears to be some overlapping scope with other proposals, how do you reconcile these?

I was not convinced this proposal needs to be included in the 2025 annual budget. Just my impression after reading it. Maybe Catalyst could provide an alternative avenue if Catalyst is approved. I appreciate your team's contributions to the Cardano space. Leaving this feedback (although generic) - just to provide some context on my temp check vote.

Thank you for your insightful questions! Please refer to the answers below;

1. How will the KPI of 10,000 USDA users be validated and measured? Will metrics such as retention rate and active usage per user also be reported?


We fully agree that measuring “user count” alone is not sufficient unless it reflects real, sustained engagement. Here’s how we plan to approach both validation and deeper usage metrics:

<KPI Measurement and Validation of 10,000 USDA Users>
We define "USDA users" as individuals who either:
1. Hold a USDA balance in a verified wallet, or
2. Have completed at least one USDA transaction (buy, transfer, or use in DeFi)

<Validation methods:>
- We will collect user-level data from integrated fintech platforms (Busha, Ejara, Nestcoin) via API or quarterly partner data reports.
- Wallet analytics tools (e.g., Cexplorer, TapTools API, custom on-chain trackers) will help cross-reference user activity.
- Where possible, user acquisition will be tagged by platform and geography, enabling region-specific validation.

<Deeper Usage Metrics (Beyond Wallet Counts)>
Yes — we will report additional quality-of-use indicators, including:
- Monthly Active Users (MAUs):
 Number of unique wallets transacting in USDA per month
- Retention Rate:
 % of users still active on the quarterly basis
- DeFi engagement rate:
 % of USDA holders who interact with Cardano-native DeFi protocols (e.g., through Nestcoin’s Onboard wallet)

These metrics will be tracked and disclosed in our Quarterly Impact Reports.

2. While quarterly impact reports are listed as a KPI, what are the criteria, format, and disclosure channels for these reports?


We consider transparency and accountability key to long-term success, especially in a region where trust-building is essential. Below is how we plan to structure our quarterly impact reporting:

<Criteria for Reporting>
Each report will track progress against six core deliverables defined in the proposal:
1. ADA Liquidity Expansion – Number of listings, volume increase (% change from baseline)
2. USDA Integration – Number of platforms integrated, wallets activated, transaction count
3. Real-World Use Cases – Remittance, savings, and bond use tracked by platform-level analytics
4. Cardano-native DeFi Access – DeFi user count, TVL in USDA, engagement via partner wallets
5. Ecosystem Awareness & Education – Events held, user engagement metrics, localization efforts
6. Quarterly Adoption Trends – Cross-cutting data from users, community, and on-chain analytics

<Format>
Reports will be structured as concise, visual PDF documents (~4–6 pages), and include:
- Executive summary
- Key performance indicators (with graphs/tables)
- Highlights of success stories and testimonials
- Partner spotlights
- On-chain data visualizations (e.g., USDA transactions, DeFi interactions)
- Lessons learned and action items for the next quarter

<Disclosure Channels>
We will share the reports through the following:
- Cardano Forum
- Adaverse websites and social media (e.g., X, LinkedIn)
- Optional: real-time dashboard for selected metrics (if resources allow)

We define a “DeFi participant” as a unique, verified user who has engaged in at least one on-chain DeFi transaction involving USDA on Cardano. This includes not just wallet connections, but actual economic interactions.

<Activities That Qualify as “DeFi Engagement”>
We will count the following USDA-based activities on Cardano as qualifying DeFi usage:
1. Lending:
 – Supplying USDA to lending pools on platforms. Potential partners considered: Aada Finance, FluidTokens, Liquid Finance and others.

2. Staking:
 – Participating in USDA staking, if offered via ecosystem partners or centralized DeFi-like interfaces (e.g., via Nestcoin Onboard).

3. Yield Farming or Liquidity Provision:
 – Providing USDA as liquidity in USDA/ADA or USDA/fiat pools
 – Claiming rewards from farming programs or AMMs. Potential partners considered: Minswap or WingRiders if/when USDA is listed.

4. Swapping & Token Interaction:
 – Executing USDA swaps via Cardano-native DEXs
 – Holding DeFi-enabled tokens received in exchange for USDA

<How DeFi Users Will Be Counted>
We will track DeFi participants using:
- On-chain data from DEX and lending protocol smart contracts
 (via address-level analytics or APIs such as TapTools, Cexplorer, and partner dashboards)
- Partner wallet analytics
 (e.g., Nestcoin’s Onboard wallet will track USDA-to-DeFi funnels)
- Minimum interaction requirement
 A user must complete at least one DeFi transaction involving USDA to be counted.
